originality_review_standard.rule: Shared topic, pathway, gene family, distractor vocabulary, or broad physiology alone is not a material duplicate. A material duplicate requires substantially the same causal mechanism/phenotype and substantially the same requested reasoning construct, even if wording is changed.
originality_review_standard.precedent: Repository commit 367e5a0c51f579d796d6385254022b62b4da16b4 rejected GNAS/PTH, MC2R/glucocorticoid-deficiency and CASR/FHH retries because they reproduced the existing causal recognition/signaling task rather than merely sharing a system.
originality_review_standard.retrieval: Exact construct-term search plus TF-IDF nearest-neighbour retrieval across all 1190 production item payloads, followed by manual adversarial construct comparison of retrieved neighbours.
originality_review_standard.limitation: Lexical similarity is retrieval evidence, not an automatic semantic originality verdict. This repository-aware review is not an independent blind Auditor execution.

Q1221.adversarial_finding: No retrieved item asks the same receptor-localization construct. The closest production items test primary thyroid feedback, peripheral GH/JAK-STAT signaling, dopamine control of prolactin, TSH/cAMP signaling, or somatostatin signaling. The repaired item asks which physiologic interaction is disrupted when a patient-derived GHRHR specifically fails to bind active GHRH.

Q1222.adversarial_finding: The high lexical overlap is real and comes from shared pancreatic beta-cell KATP physiology. Production Q0837 tests an activating KCNJ11 defect in which KATP channels remain excessively open, causing neonatal hyperglycemia and reduced insulin release; its requested construct is failure of ATP-mediated channel closure. Q1222 instead specifies biallelic ABCC8 loss of function with hypoglycemia and inappropriate insulin secretion and asks for the reduced KATP-channel activity that links the lesion to insulin excess. These are opposite functional directions, different causal genes/subunits, opposite glycemic phenotypes, and different requested lesion localization. Production Q1176 contains ABCC8 only as a distractor while testing GLUD1 hyperinsulinism. Under the repository duplicate precedent, this is same pathway family but not the same causal/requested construct.

Q1223.adversarial_finding: The GCK/glucokinase production hits occur as distractors in items testing other mechanisms. Retrieved neighbours test peripheral insulin resistance, KCNJ11 channel physiology, autoimmune beta-cell destruction, thyroid signaling or unrelated transcription factors. No production item retrieved tests heterozygous GCK loss as a beta-cell glucose-sensing defect causing stable mild familial hyperglycemia.

Q1224.adversarial_finding: Production Q0826 tests complete LEP ligand deficiency and absence of an adipocyte-derived satiety signal. Q1224 uses active ligand, preserved surface receptor abundance, preserved ligand binding, matched normal-receptor controls and selectively impaired intracellular signaling to localize a post-binding LEPR signaling defect. Same endocrine axis, different molecular lesion and different experimental localization task.

Q1225.adversarial_finding: Production Q1177 tests an activating germline LHCGR variant causing ligand-independent testosterone production and male-limited gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty; the learner identifies the diagnosis. Q1225 specifies a biallelic loss-of-function receptor shared by 46,XX and 46,XY siblings, with anovulation and Leydig-cell hypoplasia, and asks the learner to identify the receptor's two physiologic ligands, LH and hCG. This is the same locus but opposite variant direction, different inheritance/sex phenotype, and a different requested construct. Other nearest neighbours concern AMH signaling, 5-alpha-reductase deficiency or androgen-receptor defects and do not reproduce the dual-ligand LHCGR-loss task.
